title: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said the woman at the centre of the Cornell University rape case was "failed" at "every turn". The woman, known as
body: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said the woman at the centre of the Cornell University rape case was "failed" at "every turn". The woman, known as Jane Doe in legal documents, alleges she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024. The case was investigated at the time but no charges were laid. It recently reopened after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month that thrust the allegations into the national spotlight. At a news conference on Friday, Hochul said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled. She has now appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead the case. This appointment was made after Hochul said she "lost faith" in the local prosecutor's ability to oversee the investigation.Expressing outrage that local prosecutors did not interview the accuser themselves,  Hochul on Friday said: "This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and then at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her."She has also vowed to close a "loophole" that prevents prosecutors from pursuing rape charges in cases when the victim has voluntarily consumed drugs or alcohol. Jane Doe is believed to have voluntarily taken drugs and alcohol on the night of the alleged gang rape."If someone is too intoxicated to consent it should not matter if they chose to use drugs or alcohol," said Hochul, adding: "Voluntary intoxication is not a licence for gang rape."James, who is the state's chief legal officer, appeared alongside Hochul at Friday's news conference, pledging to "lead a process guided by the facts and the law".She said her office would interview witnesses and pursue prosecutions if warranted.District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who previously led the investigation, has defended his office's previous decision not to file charges in the case, arguing they were not given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold.Van Houten said much of the information released in recent weeks about the case was not passed to his office. In a statement on Friday, he said he supported James' investigation, adding: "It has become clear that we were not provided the full picture by the university."Cornell has said it provided evidence to the district attorney's office from its own investigation, including a Snapchat group chat in which fraternity members discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Doe on the night of the alleged assault.Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university in September.Speaking to CNN on Friday, her lawyer Thomas Giuffra said she is "not doing well"."She's under siege on social media, where people are trying to identify her; some false court postings, attempting to identify her," he said. Survivor and victim advocates say current state law on sexual assault makes it difficult for charges to be brought against perpetrators if the victim voluntarily took drugs or drank alcohol before the alleged assault took place.A bill to address what Hochul described as a legal loophole was already before the state legislature prior to this week's public outcry over how police and investigators handled the Cornell rape allegations. People who have voluntarily become intoxicated to the point that they are unable to give consent are currently not protected by New York's rape laws, says state assemblyman Jeffrey Dinowitz, who first sponsored legislation to close the loophole in 2019."The real bottom line is that right now if you are voluntarily intoxicated, you will not get justice," he tells BBC News. "Being voluntarily intoxicated, basically, is almost like giving somebody a get out of jail free card."Dinowitz says that around half of US states have already changed their laws to say it makes no difference whether intoxication is voluntarily or involuntarily in rape cases.Hochul said she will support the existing bill and that it could move forward as early as the next legislative session which reconvenes in January. As governor, she could also call lawmakers back for a special session before then.

schema.headline: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry 'failed' by officials, says New York governor

title: Conservatives aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference
description: When Kemi Badenoch arrived for her first Conservative conference as leader last year, a member of her entourage overheard somebody wonder aloud: "Who'
body: When Kemi Badenoch arrived for her first Conservative conference as leader last year, a member of her entourage overheard somebody wonder aloud: "Who's that?"This baffled member of the public was actually working at the Conservative conference. Badenoch had been the party's leader and the leader of the opposition for almost a year.It is an anecdote which underlines the scale of the challenge Badenoch faced at that conference, an event her allies are now with distance willing to acknowledge was make or break for her leadership.And it is an anecdote which also underlines that, far from break her, that conference represented the start of a major turnaround for Badenoch.Twelve months on, Badenoch will arrive in Birmingham this weekend in total command of a party whose leading lights are beginning to permit themselves the occasional flicker of optimism after years of misery preparing for, and then experiencing, a brutal election defeat.Yet for all that Conservatives now believe their leader is an electoral asset, they still face an existential threat from Reform UK and the challenge of how to adjust their strategy to face a new prime minister, Andy Burnham.The answer to both those issues for Badenoch is a focus on the economy. "Stronger economy, stronger country" will be the party's conference slogan, with the two speeches Badenoch gives - one on Sunday, the other on Wednesday - building on announcements she has made in the past two weeks about cutting benefits for the long-term unemployed.Welfare spending is increasingly seen by the Conservatives as a core battleground with Labour.During Labour conference they derided the event as the "Welfare Party Conference". Whereas Sir Keir Starmer sought to cut welfare spending before backing down in the face of a rebellion by his own MPs, Burnham has made clear that he believes the way to reduce the benefits bill in the long-term is more up-front investment in support for those out of work.This is a clear ideological difference which both parties are happy to embrace. Conservative strategists believe there is a broader lesson there. "The differences between the parties have been quite muddled for a while," one says. "Now that Burnham is prime minister we have a more traditional left-right split."Another area where Badenoch will embrace that divide in the coming days is the pensions triple-lock.The policy currently guarantees the state pension goes up each year in line with either inflation, wage increases, or 2.5% – whichever is the highest.Badenoch will make clear that the Conservatives continue to support that policy in its current form, breaking with some generally supportive think tanks and policy experts who believe Badenoch should follow Burnham's lead.In his conference speech on Tuesday, Burnham set out plans to end the existing triple lock from 2030, so the state pension increases at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.The Conservatives hope the sharpening left-right split leaves Reform UK in a strategic bind, occupying a less obvious place on that spectrum. A year ago some senior Conservatives feared being usurped by Reform as the leading party of the right was a near-inevitability, but now they are optimistic that Nigel Farage's party is on an inexorable slide.That bullishness is fuelled in large part by the difficulties Reform has faced over Nigel Farage's £5m gift from Christopher Harborne and the fallout - including a police inquiry - from the recent Channel 4 News investigation."I find more and more voters raise concerns about Reform with me - people who weren't previously giving us the time of day," one MP said. "These are successful people with big garages and good jobs who do not necessarily pay that much attention but want a small-c conservative government."They were switching to Reform because they were fed up with us and thought Farage was now the main option on the right. But they are starting to come back."Others are less positive, pointing out that Reform still often record higher shares than the Conservatives in the polls  — and more importantly have now won far more votes than them in successive years of local and national elections.Whether or not there is indeed a long-term trend of the Conservatives regaining ground at Reform's expense, Badenoch may not have long enough to wait. She has told her team to prepare for this conference as if it is the last before the general election. While not all of her aides agree, Badenoch is convinced that Burnham will go to the polls within the next year.Party high command started weekly election planning meetings shortly after Burnham succeeded Starmer. Neil O'Brien, a member of Badenoch's shadow cabinet, has begun work on a manifesto alongside the party's head of policy. It is intended to be a more concise set of pledges than the usual sprawling manifestos.Also with an eye to the election, the Conservatives will present new faces at the conference who have applied to be candidates at the next election. Badenoch's ambivalence in some cases, and opposition in others, to ex-MPs who lost their seats in 2024 standing for the party again has attracted some controversy, especially when it comes to the high-profile former cabinet ministers Grant Shapps and Penny Mordaunt.The leader's supporters are unrepentant, arguing that the party "needs to show we have changed".Things have certainly changed since last year, at least. That may prove the easy part.

schema.headline: Conservatives aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

title: Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after botched execution, lawyer says
description: Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.Hospital staff are working to s
body: Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.Hospital staff are working to save her life and clear the drug used, pentobarbital, from her system, the filing states.During the execution attempt, prison officials tried to start intravenous (IV) lines by using at least seven needles on Pike, according to her lawyers.At one point, Pike herself offered guidance of where they could try."One needle was bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," the filing states.While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review into Pike's botched execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.The state's department of correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have not not offered any explanations about what went wrong.Pike's attorneys previously warned that her conditions, including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.In the latest filings, her lawyers allege that "at no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike's body".They are requesting that all relevant physical, written and electronic evidence is preserved.Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team, said two doses of pentobarbital was enough that "she would have surely died" had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation.The only possible explanation for her survival, Zivot said, "is that the pentobarbital blood level was never high enough to cause death" and that blisters on her arm after the botched execution indicated a ruptured vein.So, instead of entering Pike's bloodstream, he said, the pentobarbital was more likely to have spread across the tissue under her skin.Pike's medical condition of thrombocytosis may have also played a role, forming blood clots at the injection site that would potentially block pentobarbital from entering her veins.Regarding the possibility the pentobarbital was degraded, Zivot explained that if this was the case, it could be due to factors including poor manufacturing or improper storage.

schema.headline: Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after botched execution, lawyer says

title: What we know about the Cornell University frat house rape investigation
description: Figure caption, Cornell students voice frustration at public hearing over rape caseByNardine SaadKayla Epstein and Nada TawfikNorth America correspond
body: Figure caption, Cornell students voice frustration at public hearing over rape caseByNardine SaadKayla Epstein and Nada TawfikNorth America correspondentReporting fromat Cornell UniversityUpdated 4 hours agoNew York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into the alleged rape of a woman at Cornell University in 2024.The woman, identified anonymously as Jane Doe in court documents, filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university this month alleging she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house at the university.She also alleged that Cornell failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.Cornell has said it supported presenting the case to a grand jury, while rejecting claims it failed to punish those involved. Here's what we know.Figure caption, Watch: Why an investigation into alleged frat house gang rape is reopeningWhat does the woman allege?Jane Doe alleges in her civil lawsuit that, on the night of 19 October 2024, seven men from Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity chapter assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine. She was a 20-year-old Cornell undergraduate at the time.Jane Doe said in her lawsuit that she was intoxicated during the alleged incident and could not provide consent.She said she left her sorority sisters after drinking that night and "stumbled alone" to the Chi Phi fraternity house in the city of Ithaca to see a male friend.The lawsuit alleges sexual assault and battery, negligence, breach of contract and violations of New York's Human Rights Law.It was filed against the university, fraternity sorority and men involved in the alleged attack, who have been dubbed the "Cornell Seven".Doe also alleges that the men were "afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays". Doe's lawyer has said she was "traumatised, numb and unable to function or accept the horror of what had happened" in the days after the assault, which she reported to Cornell University Police on 8 November 2024.The attorney has said two of those involved were expelled. He told CBS the accuser dropped out of university after the alleged assault. Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Cornell in Ithaca, New York, is an elite US universityWhat was in the fraternity Snapchat and text messages?Jane Doe's lawsuit contains an image purported to be from a fraternity group chat in which a participant alerted other members, in vulgar terms, to the potential for a sexual encounter with Doe.Cornell University said its police department provided an image of the Snapchat group, titled Chi Phi Actives, to prosecutors as evidence in November 2024.The members are named in the chat and discuss a "free" sexual encounter with Jane Doe, using coarse language, in the early hours of 20 October 2024.CBS News New York has also published excerpts of additional text messages reportedly exchanged between one of the defendants and a woman who appears to be Jane Doe.The messages were reportedly sent two days after the alleged assault.In one message, one of the men appeared to apologise for "how things went down". He said his memory was "kinda fuzzy", and that he and another man felt bad for being too intoxicated to "shut it down and kick people out before it got way out of hand".The woman in the text chain replied saying her memory was "super clouded too" and that they were all intoxicated.She also wrote that "non(e) of the sexual stuff was illegal" and that she liked being with him and another man.Doe suggested they smoke together again but leave out "the extra five billion men and ketamine".Image source, ReutersImage caption, Cornell University's Chi Phi fraternity house in September 2026How did Cornell respond?Doe said she reported the incident to Cornell University Police two weeks after it happened.Shortly afterwards, Cornell University issued a public statement regarding the allegations, which it called "serious and deeply disturbing". It said the campus police department was investigating and that it had suspended the local chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity, as well as "a number of students".Cornell also said it had opened an internal investigation, as well as a civil rights inquiry under the Title IX law, which bars sex discrimination in schools that receive funding from the federal government, including most universities.Following the new lawsuit, the university disputed Doe's allegation that it did not adequately investigate or punish the alleged perpetrators.The university said the matter was referred to a "panel of trained faculty and staff" that issued "a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions from Cornell".Cornell did not deny the punishment for some of those involved included writing an essay.On 1 October, New York state Governor Kathy Hochul appointed state Attorney General Letitia James to take over the investigation, replacing Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten.James said she would review evidence and pursue prosecutions if necessary.The governor also vowed to close a legal loophole allowing offenders to avoid rape charges if their victims were willingly intoxicated.What has the fraternity said?Doe named Chi Phi fraternity as one of the defendants in her civil lawsuit, alleging she suffered physical and emotional damage as a result of their actions.Trey Robb, interim executive director of the Chi Phi fraternity, said the organisation had expelled the accused members of Cornell's chapter."Our records confirm that just three days after 'Jane Doe' filed a police report, the Xi chapter voted unanimously to remove the accused members from its rolls," Robb said. "The chapter also recommended that our national fraternity permanently expel them, and our Grand Council did so at a subsequent meeting."The Xi Chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity was closed in 2024 and remains barred from campus.Why were no charges brought in 2024?Van Houten, the county's top prosecutor, said on Monday that his office would reopen a criminal inquiry into the alleged rape.He said that at the time of the alleged assault two years ago his office concluded that evidence did not meet the legal bar to bring charges.Van Houten included a summary of what Doe told the Cornell University Police Department in 2024 after the alleged attack, noting it differed from the allegations laid out in the lawsuit."Jane Doe's sworn statement in November of 2024 did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped," Van Houten said in a statement on Monday."On the contrary, Jane Doe's statement described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious and consensual."Figure caption, "I'm very shocked" - College students react to Cornell University rape investigationNew reports have detailed what Doe reported to Cornell University's police following the incident.CBS News New York, external obtained a transcript of Doe's interviews with campus police that began on 14 November - more than three weeks after the incident.She tells police of the initial sexual encounter: "I was pretty OK with all of this."But the outlet reports that she said of what happened later: "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped."The district attorney told CBS News he had never seen the transcript of the interview with campus police.Van Houten told the BBC he had only received a signed shorter statement from the alleged victim and a screenshot of the Snapchat messages. Initially, Cornell University said, external it had shared "all investigatory information" with the  district attorney's office.But it later changed its statement to say it had shared the accuser's statement and the Snapchat messages. In a statement to the BBC, Cornell said its page providing information on its response is "a living document, and we are working to update it regularly". ABC News, external also obtained a police report from 15 November, in which Doe said that, during one of the later encounters that night: "I felt like I was unable to make any decision because of how intoxicated I was."If you are suffering distress or despair and need support, you could speak to a health professional, or an organisation that offers support. Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide., externalA list of UK organisations that can help is available here.

schema.headline: What we know about the Cornell University frat house rape investigation

title: Royal Navy's new attack submarine arrives at Faslane
description: Image source, Royal NavyImage caption, HMS Agamemnon arrived on the River Clyde after departing BarrowThe Royal Navy's newest Astute-class nuclear-pow
body: Image source, Royal NavyImage caption, HMS Agamemnon arrived on the River Clyde after departing BarrowThe Royal Navy's newest Astute-class nuclear-powered submarine has arrived at its home port in Scotland.HMS Agamemnon will undergo sea trials and operational preparation after reaching HM Naval Base Clyde at Faslane.The hunter-killer vessel, the sixth in the Navy's arsenal, is equipped with tomahawk land-attack missiles and torpedoes capable of striking targets up to 30 miles away.The Navy's submarine rear admiral, Andy Perks, described HMS Agamemnon's arrival as a "significant milestone".The 318ft-long (97m) vessel joins other Astute-class subs including HMS Astute, Ambush, Artful, Audacious and Anson, in the Navy's fleet.A seventh sub, HMS Achilles, is currently under construction.Astute-class submarines are the Navy's most advanced and powerful class of attack subs.Image source, Royal NavyImage caption, The Astute-class sub conducted its first dive at sea on the journey to FaslaneHMS Agamemnon departed its construction home at BAE systems in Barrow last week and went through its first dive at sea in the Navy's Inner Hebrides exercise areas en-route.Rear admiral Perks said: "HMS Agamemnon's delivery reflects the dedication, skill and collaboration of thousands of people across our Defence Nuclear Enterprise, who have worked together to build one of the world's most capable attack submarines and deliver a formidable warfighting capability for the United Kingdom."I am delighted to welcome the submarine and her ship's company to their new home on the Clyde, and I look forward to seeing them join the operational fleet in due course."Image source, Royal NavyImage caption, The Astute-class fleet are the Navy's most powerful and technologically advanced attack subsThe vessel, which has a crew of about 100 submariners, will have its performance tested during sea trials over the coming months.Its arrival coincided with the 125th anniversary of the launch of Holland 1, the Royal Navy's first submarine..HMS Agamemnon's commanding officer, commander John Gabb, said: "It is an enormous privilege to be the first person to command this vessel at sea."We will get to know Agamemnon well over the coming months, but this submarine is incredibly quiet, has a world-class Sonar and will be home to us all as we generate for operations."

schema.headline: Royal Navy's new attack submarine arrives at Faslane

title: Rui Pinto: Hacker who released Man City documents fears for life as he prepares to lose witness protection
description: Pinto became part of Portugal's witness protection programme in 2020 after agreeing to co-operate with authorities and provide files obtained through
body: Pinto became part of Portugal's witness protection programme in 2020 after agreeing to co-operate with authorities and provide files obtained through the Football Leaks operation.He posted on X on Friday, external that the decision to terminate his participation in the programme on 10 October has put him in a "life-threatening situation".The 37-year-old said it had left him with no alternative but to relocate to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period because of "multiple death threats" and "the serious risk of an assassination attempt".BBC Sport has approached the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Crimes in Portugal for comment.Pinto has described himself as a whistleblower, but was convicted in Portugal of offences including illegal access to data and attempted extortion and given a four-year suspended sentence.He wore a bulletproof vest during his first trial in 2020, which was also subject to heightened security measures.Earlier this year, he was acquitted in a second trial of 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to a number of sports bodies in Portugal, including Benfica.On Wednesday, Pinto turned his attention to Fifa president Gianni Infantino, saying he had "become a cancer on football" and should "have no place in the future of the game".Pinto repeated allegations from 2018 that Infantino intervened to help City and Paris St-Germain avoid financial fair play sanctions from European football's governing body Uefa.Infantino's position has recently come under increased pressure following controversial plans to sell stakes in the governing body's competitions, such as the World Cup, to private investors. A statement from Pinto's lawyers released on Friday said the decision to end his participation in the witness protection programme left him at heightened risk, noting legal proceedings stemming from the leaks remained ongoing, including the case against Manchester City.Pinto has set up a fundraising page to help him "survive this serious situation", which he claims was "created by the Portuguese State".

schema.headline: Rui Pinto: Hacker who released Man City documents fears for life as he prepares to lose witness protection

title: Beijing Open: Aryna Sabalenka 'expects a bit more from myself' after win over Renata Zarazua
description: Aryna Sabalenka said she was "trying so hard to be easier on myself" as she began her China Open campaign with victory over Renata Zarazua.World numbe
body: Aryna Sabalenka said she was "trying so hard to be easier on myself" as she began her China Open campaign with victory over Renata Zarazua.World number two Sabalenka hit 11 aces and did not face a break point in a 6-1 6-3 victory over the Mexican.The Belarusian needed just 63 minutes to win her first match since losing her world number one ranking and her US Open crown to Elena Rybakina in September.The 28-year-old is bidding for her first title since completing the 'Sunshine Double' in March, when she won Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.It has been a mixed year for Sabalenka by her high standards. She will finish without a Grand Slam trophy for the first time since 2022 and has often struggled to control her frustrations on court.Asked about being so self-critical, Sabalenka said: "I think this is a good and a bad side of my personality, that I always ask and wait for more from myself. "Sometimes it can drive me forward, but sometimes it can really drain my energy."Maybe this is something I have to finally learn. I'm really trying so hard sometimes to be easier on myself."Sabalenka will face Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova - who came close to beating her at the Berlin Open in June - in the third round.Top seed Rybakina begins her campaign at the WTA 1000 event on Saturday.Earlier, Britain's Katie Boulter fell 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 to Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova, while French Open champion Mirra Andreeva recovered to beat Chinese wildcard Yuan Yue 3-6 6-0 6-0.In the men's event, sixth seed Daniil Medvedev produced 12 aces to beat Spain's Pablo Carreno Busta 6-4 6-2.British pair Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool advanced in the doubles, beating Russia's Andrey Rublev and Karen Khachanov 6-3 6-4.

schema.headline: Beijing Open: Aryna Sabalenka 'expects a bit more from myself' after win over Renata Zarazua

title: Ukraine 0-3 Northern Ireland: Who has 'no ceiling' as Michael O'Neill's side shine?
description: Michael O'Neill had spent the build-up to Northern Ireland's Nations League outing against Ukraine playing down memories of their famous win at Euro 2
body: Michael O'Neill had spent the build-up to Northern Ireland's Nations League outing against Ukraine playing down memories of their famous win at Euro 2016.His focus was firmly on what was to come rather than reflect on the past.If a stunning 3-0 victory on Friday night was anything to go by, it's going to be a pretty exciting future indeed.His starting team had an average age of just 22, which was the youngest on record for Northern Ireland since World War Two.Oxford's Ciaron Brown, the only player over the age of 25 to start the game in Trnava, Slovakia, was in the right place to open the scoring in the ninth minute from Ruairi McConville's knockdown.O'Neill handed a first start to 19-year-old Kieran Morrison, and his superb cross led to Isaac Price doubling the lead, before Brown's header evaded goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk in bizarre circumstances with 30 minutes left.While the victory may not be quite as memorable as the 2-0 'Kings of Lyon' success 10 years ago at the Euros, it was extremely impressive.To put it into context - and never mind the manner of the performance - only Sweden and France have beaten Ukraine in the past 12 months.Northern Ireland can now be added to that list.Brown's two goals were just reward for a player who has been quietly impressive for far longer than this campaign, and he was part of a back-five which stood out in what was a third consecutive clean sheet. Brodie Spencer and Terry Devlin were drafted in at the full-back positions and both impressed, but Brown's centre-back partners McConville and Tom Atcheson really shone.Norwich City defender McConville, 21, commanded his area well and, as well as an assist for Brown, he also allowed the ball to trickle over the line when he could have touched home for the third goal instead of his team-mate.Atcheson, himself only 20 and playing for Blackburn Rovers in the Championship, made his Northern Ireland debut in Wales in March, but showed composure beyond his years.O'Neill said both players were "terrific" as he told BBC Sport: "They have no ceiling, to be honest."They are both playing in the Championship at the minute but they are ready to go to the next level."They will make mistakes at times and we've put a lot on them in terms of the physicality. The two of them were brilliant."O'Neill was also delighted for Brown, who said he had "really grown" into a senior role in the absence of injured Sunderland defender Dan Ballard."Three 90 minutes at this level is tough," said O'Neill of the 28-year-old."He plays his club football in League One and he's a better player than that."He brings a lot to the team. He was our most senior player tonight and he has really grown into that."If they can end the quadruple-header unbeaten they will head into November's final two matches on a high, and the wider implications are significant.Topping the group would seal promotion to League A for the first time, and mean Northern Ireland will be in a five-team group for Euro 2028 qualification, with a potential fall-back of a play-off should the campaign go awry.They had not won an away Nations League match before Shea Charles' 99th-minute winner in Georgia, and this was their biggest away success in five years.Former international Stephen Craigan, on co-commentary in Slovakia, described it as potentially "a seismic night" for a young group, which was missing Ballard, the influential Ethan Galbraith and Liverpool defender Conor Bradley, while Justin Devenny started on the bench.The real implications of the victory may only become clear further down the line, but all focus for now will be on the recovery before the final game of the window on Monday. "There is a big togetherness in a young group," said the 23-year-old Price, who scored his first international goal in just over a year."We're loving it and we love coming away. It's about building momentum and we're doing that."

schema.headline: Ukraine 0-3 Northern Ireland: Who has 'no ceiling' as Michael O'Neill's side shine?

title: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
description: Spain's Congress has rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis, in a defeat for the government of Pedro Sánchez tha
body: Spain's Congress has rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis, in a defeat for the government of Pedro Sánchez that increases pressure on him to call a snap election.Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by the government in response to nationwide protests that have followed the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, from her home. The decrees, which introduced a series of initiatives aimed at protecting tenants in the rental market, required parliamentary approval in order to remain in place.MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.Hundreds of demonstrators had gathered outside Congress as the debate took place and there were angry scenes. Protesters chanted "shame on you" and "your profits, our misery", after the results were announced.The government's defeat underlines the fact that Sánchez, a Socialist, does not command a congressional majority and it has heightened speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer. Sources told Spanish media that the government would spend the weekend deciding its next step, and whether to dissolve parliament.Sánchez's beleaguered government had already been mired in a series of scandals and judicial cases affecting his Socialist Party and close allies.The Sindicato de Inquilinas (Tenants' Union) activist association which has been co-ordinating protests, announced during the congressional debate that it was abandoning the tent protest in central Madrid. It said it wanted to "take the struggle to all the neighbourhoods, residential blocks and homes of Madrid, wherever there are rental increases, expulsions and abuses each day, and turn the energy of the last few days into a permanent organisation".Protesters are also calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.The left-wing coalition government responded to the social anger by hurriedly drawing up the two decree-laws in an effort to defuse the protests.The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Sindicato de Inquilinas.The conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country. However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.Friday's debate was fierce and at times angry, as supporters and opponents of the decrees clashed in Congress."I don't ask you, I beg you to be brave and consistent," Sánchez said, moments before the two votes took place. "Because they are not just ambitious measures, they are necessary". He appealed to lawmakers "to put order and humanity into [the housing] market, because if we don't, it will bring down our society".Social Affairs minister Pablo Bustinduy, of the Sumar alliance, the junior partner in the governing coalition, presented the debate in dramatic terms."Today is about defending an international oligarchy which is extracting the rent from salaries earned with the effort of working classes of this country in order to share it out with dividends and they don't even pay taxes in Spain," he said. "Voting against these decrees today means defending the interests of this oligarchy and turning your back on your own people."However, Miriam Nogueras, of JxCat, said the decrees had been hastily drawn up and lacked rigour. She said the decrees "will allow [vulture] funds to keep buying, keep speculating and evictions to keep happening… these two decrees would provoke the opposite effect of what they aim to achieve."The political right has argued that the government's attempts to intervene will frighten homeowners, causing them not to put their properties on the rental market and pushing prices up further.Juan Bravo of the PP said "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

schema.headline: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87

title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
description: The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to gover
body: The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.The party said it would cost £2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "A violent criminal doesn't become less dangerous just because the government has run out of prison cells."She added: "[Labour's] answer is to let dangerous offenders out even earlier instead of building the prison spaces we need."Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said: "The Tories are taking the public for fools. Across 14 years in government, they added just 500 prison places and closed 23 prisons. "Now Kemi Badenoch expects the British people to believe they'll build 50,000."Meanwhile, the Prison Governors' Association said "long-term investment" was needed and warned a "staffing crisis" would pose challenges to delivering new prisons.If the party wins power, the Tories said they would introduce legislation early in the new Parliament to override planning and procurement barriers, allowing the process to be "fast-tracked".It said the use of private finance would help speed up delivery and control costs.There are currently around 89,000 useable prison places in England and Wales, according to the latest government figures.The Tories said their proposals would increase this figure by more than 50%, with the vast majority of new places expected within the party's first Parliament in government - up to five years - and the full increase delivered within seven years.The £2bn a year cost would be funded through savings in other areas, including cutting the aid budget by £1bn and reducing the budget of the Department for Culture Media and Sport by £1bn.The Labour government has promised to add 14,000 extra prison space by 2031.The Tories argued increasing prison places would cut crime and prevent reoffending by keeping serious criminals off the streets.Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said: "Prison works. It works by punishing and deterring, but most importantly by incapacitating. "Prison should keep violent and repeat offenders away from the law-abiding public."

schema.headline: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places

title: Man City guilty charges: Which clubs did 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?
description: Manchester City's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant pric
body: Manchester City's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant prices rose for everybody else too.And once the world knows that a club has a wedge of cash burning a hole in its pocket courtesy of City, it can be difficult to spend it.Asking prices may rise, and having an influx of money is no guarantee of it being well spent.For many of the teams to whom City paid the most during this time, the money did not work out particularly beneficially.Let's take a look at some of the more interesting cases.First up, Wolfsburg. They immediately signed winger Julian Draxler for about half the fee received for Kevin de Bruyne in 2016, as well as others including veteran defender Dante.Having lost De Bruyne, they dropped from second to eighth in the Bundesliga before narrowly avoiding relegation in the subsequent two seasons.And things did not go particularly well for second highest-ranked club Monaco either. The most direct replacements they signed following the sales of Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva in the same summer to Manchester City - Terence Kongolo and Keita Balde - did not work out in the long run, and the team went from winning Ligue 1 and reaching the Champions League semi-finals to almost being relegated within two years.The club City purchased most players from in the 2009-18 period - Arsenal (four) - did not mount a serious Premier League title challenge during that time.Some clubs who did not receive payments from City could also argue that the spending of money from their "inflated" accounts compromised their chances.For example, Manchester City paid very similar totals to Benfica and Porto during the era, but nothing to Sporting, the club which makes up the big three in Portugal.Sporting did not win a title between 2009 and 2018. There are many reasons for that, but could one of them be the fact that their direct rivals received money from City that would perhaps not have been on offer had they followed football's financial rules?There are also some ancillary fees which reached clubs whom Manchester City did not deal with directly.Some players were subject to sell-on clauses, where the club City where buying the player from owed money to the previous team who owned the player.For example, Queens Park Rangers earned roughly £9m from Raheem Sterling's move to City from Liverpool in 2015.Barnsley took about £7m of the transfer fee paid to Everton for John Stones in 2016, and the Toffees also had to pass on about £2.5m to Wolves when Joleon Lescott moved to Manchester in 2009.The Sterling and Stones clauses were worth more than most players operating in the English Football League at that time, significantly strengthening the financial positions of QPR and Barnsley.To this day Barnsley have not sold a player for a higher amount than the fee they are believed to have received for Stones.But QPR have not returned to the Premier League and Barnsley dropped down to League One from the Championship after two seasons.Manchester City's spending during the time in which they were breaking the rules certainly had an enormous impact, on their own upward trajectory, the futures of other clubs around the world and the wider football economy.But the reality is that it is impossible to unweave the tapestry of football history during that time and since - too much has happened and there are too many indirect consequences.The effects of that spending will reverberate for years to come.

schema.headline: Man City guilty charges: Which clubs did 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?

title: Super League Grand Final: Warrington and Wakefield battle to be winner number six
description: While this is Wakefield's first final and the same for many of their players, like coach Powell a select few have sampled the unique atmosphere of Old
body: While this is Wakefield's first final and the same for many of their players, like coach Powell a select few have sampled the unique atmosphere of Old Trafford for Super League's showpiece event.Tom Johnstone begrudgingly left Wakefield for Catalans in 2023 and reached the Grand Final in his first season, before rejoining Trinity in 2025.That night ended in disappointment with defeat by Wigan, so the 2026 final represents a second chance for the England winger to pick up the ring he so covets - although it will not be the most important ring in his life as he admits."It's going to be different in so many ways for me because as much as I loved Catalans, this is my team," Johnstone told BBC Radio 5 live."This has been my team for almost all of my career, and the team that gave me an opportunity 15 years ago as a youngster."So, this is special, this is the big one and it's probably going to be, if we get it done, the best night of my life. Sorry, after my wedding, my wife said. She said it has to be second to my wedding."Like Warrington, Wakefield have waited a long time to return to league glory, with a 58-year gap since their last title.That narrative is one of many utilised by both clubs as inspiration for this Grand Final encounter, with several on both sides.One story for Wakefield to thrive upon is the impending retirement of stalwart back-rower Jay Pitts.Born in Ossett and a graduate of the youth set-up at Wakefield, the 36-year-old has amassed just short of 200 appearances for Trinity across two spells bookending his career which will end once Saturday's final is done.Pitts has battled through this crucial period following a bicep injury, and his determination and leadership are integral to the spirit within the dressing room."After the Wigan game I just went into the changing rooms and said to him 'you know you get to play your final game at Old Trafford'. It's what dreams are made of," Powell added."While there's a few players leaving us for different reasons, for Pittsy retiring after his final game in rugby league - what better way for us all to do something special for him as a person?"He's been a phenomenal player, a warrior, and I know all the boys love him. He gets a fair bit of stick for how old he is but that comes to us all so I won't worry about that too much."It has been 71 years since Warrington last won a league title and it is their first trip to Old Trafford for eight years.In the Super League era, the Wire have now reached five Grand Finals, but are yet to cross the line and write their name on the trophy.For Ben Currie, he is acutely aware of the gap between trophies, having been with the club during their four other visits - albeit he is yet to actually a appear in a Grand Final."It's hard not to know about it when you've got the opposite fans singing about it every week," he told BBC Radio Merseyside."Obviously it's tongue in cheek and it's fun for the fans to do that."We'd love to give our fans the opportunity to sing back to them but there's no added pressure from anyone from above in the club, from the coaching staff or from the senior players."Everyone wants it just the same as everyone does at Wakefield."One member of the Warrington team who could make an impact is 18-year-old Ewan Irwin.Since making his debut in 2025, Irwin has gone on to make 21 appearances this season, scoring six tries and kicking 82 goals.Matty Ashton, who himself was a bright young prospect for the Wire not so long ago, spoke highly of his team-mate, who has the chance to become the youngest player to ever score in a Grand Final."You see him day in and day out, his work ethic, he's probably the best I've seen in a young lad [and] obviously I've been at the club for seven years," Ashton said of Irwin to BBC Radio Merseyside."The way he's willing to learn when he speaks to leaders like George [Williams], it's just great to see."He's just got that something, you can see it. Obviously I don't want to put too much pressure as he's my team-mate, but he'll go all the way and he's got a big chance to do something like that."Warrington name a squad with just one change in their line-up.Jordy Crowther comes into the squad, with Max Wood dropping out.Wakefield, meanwhile, are unchanged following their dramatic semi-final win against Wigan Warriors.Josh Rourke is once again named in their provisional squad as he continues his return from a knee injury sustained in August.Warrington (from): Taylor-Wray, Thewlis, King, Hopoate, Ashton, Williams, Yates, Walker, Harrison, Stone, Currie, Powell, Byrne, Crowther, Irwin, Hayes, Bentley, Philbin, Lindop, Smith, Tanginoa.Wakefield (from): Jowitt, Scott, Hall, Johnstone, Trueman, Lino, McMeeken, Smoothy, Rodwell, Tevaga, Pitts, Hamlin-Uele, Faatili, Smith, Vagana, Walmsley, Sinfield, Myers, Rourke, Lolesio, Lipowicz.

title: Man jailed for piloting small boat carrying 26 others to Kent coast
description: A man has been jailed for 18 months for piloting a small boat carrying 26 other people, including six children, towards the Kent coast. Jemal Abdela,
body: A man has been jailed for 18 months for piloting a small boat carrying 26 other people, including six children, towards the Kent coast. Jemal Abdela, 32, was sentenced after pleading guilty to the offence of endangering others during a sea crossing to the UK without valid entry clearance on July 25.Winchester Crown Court heard Abdela, who is Eritrean, had also attempted to disguise the fact he had been driving the black inflatable across the Channel when it was approached by immigration officers.A Home Office spokesman said Abdela was the 20th small boat pilot to be imprisoned in four months for endangering lives at sea.Matthew Parris, prosecuting, told the court that the defendant was seen piloting the boat, which was being followed by French authorities.He said Abdela had "dived into the centre of the boat and moved to another location wearing a hat" before being identified, adding that the vessel did not have flares, GPS or maps onboard.The court heard that Abdela told police he had paid €800 (£680) for the crossing, which had begun at 17:00 BST the previous day.He also claimed to have been sat by the captain of the boat, but was then made to take over control of the vessel by the other passengers.Francesca Hallett, defending, said that Abdela had managed to "escape" war-torn Eritrea, where he was born.She said that he first went to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, but was imprisoned because of his Eritrean nationality.He then went on to travel through Sudan and Egypt to Libya where he was captured and tortured by people smugglers for eight months and was later freed.Hallett added that Abdela moved on to Italy and France, both of which he described as "not safe for refugees"."At that stage he felt the UK was the safest option," she said.Sentencing Abdela, Judge James Bromige said that he would "ordinarily" be deported on completion of his time in prison.Anna Turley, Minister for Border Security and Asylum, called Abdela a "reckless criminal" who had been "rightly jailed".Additional reporting by PA Media Follow BBC Kent on Facebook, external,  X, external, and on Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Kent on Sounds. Send your story ideas to southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk, external or WhatsApp us on 08081 002250.

title: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat
description: The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in a bid to ease supply pressures that have caused prices to skyrocket.The group of
body: The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in a bid to ease supply pressures that have caused prices to skyrocket.The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would include a "substantial release" of diesel in the coming days.President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports in a move which would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.In a joint statement, the G7 said member countries had now agreed to "refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products" on one another.The G7 includes the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France, with the EU also represented at its meetings.Trump had warned he would ban diesel exports from the US if European countries did not agree to put more of their own stocks onto the market.On Friday, he said on social media: "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."His Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had argued US farmers, truckers, and businesses "should not be left carrying the burden" as prices soar.Diesel is used heavily by the haulage industry and in agriculture, meaning rises in the cost of the fuel feed through into essentials such as food.But, following a meeting of G7 leaders, French President Emmanuel Macron said the bloc had agreed to release reserves of "up to 100 million barrels" within four months under the coordination of the International Energy Agency (IEA).The UK was represented at the meeting by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who said the measures would "stabilise energy supplies, build resilience in supply chains and shield households and businesses from price shocks".Macron said the coordinated action would "bring down the prices of petroleum products, particularly diesel". Highlighting the agreement not to pursue export bans, Macron said "President Trump, in particular, was very clear on this point". Speaking at the White House, Trump later said an export ban on diesel was "never really on the table". In the joint statement, G7 leaders said: "We will implement our commitments with a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners." It is not yet clear which partner countries will release stocks, nor how quickly.The 100 million barrels will comprise a mix of diesel and crude oil. The price of global benchmark Brent crude oil briefly dropped below $100 a barrel, but rose back to around $102 by Friday evening. Before the US and Israel invaded Iran, it was trading at around $73.Matt Smith, director of commodities research at Kpler, said oil had risen again due to renewed strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen."Oil prices were selling off strongly due to the announcement of strategic stock releases in Europe, but they reversed course on rumours of Saudi Arabia planning an offensive into Yemen as it looks to re-establish a safe path via Bab-Al Mandeb," he said.European countries had pushed back against US threats to turn off American diesel, against a backdrop of the US-led war in the Middle East and reduced supplies from Russia and China.The G7 leaders said they will also coordinate maintenance schedules to avoid multiple refineries being shut down at the same time, while encouraging countries with the capacity to do so to ramp up refining of diesel in particular. Supplies of diesel internationally have been heavily constrained by the conflict in the Middle East, which has restricted the flow of both crude oil and refined diesel onto global markets.Russia, which is also a major producer, has implemented its own export ban on diesel, following attacks on its refineries by Ukraine, further limiting supply. The G7 leaders stressed that they will maintain sanctions against Russia amid its ongoing war in Ukraine. Diesel is harder to refine than petrol and, because of its use in the haulage industry and agriculture, it is very difficult to reduce demand.

schema.headline: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat

title: Former priest Chris Brain guilty of raping and assaulting women
description: A former priest who established a "cult" within the Church of England has been found guilty of raping a woman in his congregation.Chris Brain was also
body: A former priest who established a "cult" within the Church of England has been found guilty of raping a woman in his congregation.Chris Brain was also convicted of four counts of indecent assault against three other women who were part of the Nine O'Clock Service in Sheffield in the 1980s and 1990s.The 69-year-old was found guilty of the offences after a retrial at Inner London Crown Court, having already been found guilty of 17 indecent assaults against nine women at a trial last year.Brain, previously of Wilmslow, in Cheshire, is in custody awaiting sentencing at a later date.The Nine O'Clock Service, known as NOS, attracted hundreds of young people to St Thomas's church with its ground-breaking nightclub-style worship which blended rave culture, live music and prayer.But jurors heard the group "became a cult" in which members were encouraged to cut themselves off from family and friends, leaving them "utterly dependent" on Brain, and living in fear of being ostracised if they crossed him.Prosecutor Tim Clark KC told the court Brain had abused his position as a priest to sexually assault "a staggering number of women from his congregation".The verdicts mean Brain has now been convicted of a total of 22 sexual offences against 13 women.Following his latest convictions, South Yorkshire Police said Brain was a "devious and arrogant sexual predator who caused lasting harm to these women".Across the two trials the court heard several of Brain's victims were part of a so-called "homebase team", who cared for him 24 hours a day in his family home and would be expected to "put him to bed" with sexual massages.One woman told the court how Brain had pushed her down onto his bed and raped her after inviting her to his house while his wife was away between 1981 and 1984.Another victim said in evidence at both trials she was sexually assaulted by the priest in her bedroom while traumatised after spending hours helping people at the Hillsborough disaster locate the bodies of friends and family.Brain, who quit as a priest when allegations about his conduct were first publicly raised in 1995, accepted having sexual contact with some of the women but told the court it had always been consensual.In an Everyman Special documentary broadcast by BBC One in November 1995, Brain admitted sexual activity with women members of NOS but denied it was abuse and said it was for "closeness and affection", the court heard.In a statement released after Friday's verdicts, one of Brain's victims from the first trial said she and the other women had waited more than 30 years for justice, adding the delay should be a "cause of great shame for the Church of England".She said church leaders had "ignored warning signs" about Brain and "utterly failed in their duty of care"."Our continued healing is not dependent on this guilty verdict," the woman said.  "But at last the immense pain this man inflicted has been acknowledged, he is finally accountable and we can continue to move forward."She added: "This group of women are without doubt the best, bravest and smartest women you could ever know and I am so very proud of us all."Brain's trials heard at least two members of clergy had raised concerns about him with the Diocese of Sheffield years before he was stopped.After Brain was first convicted in August 2025, the Bishop of Sheffield, the Rt Rev Dr Pete Wilcox, apologised for "institutional failures" and announced an independent safeguarding into its response.In a statement following the latest verdicts on Friday, he said: "My first thoughts today are with the women whose courage brought this retrial to a conclusion. They have now given evidence, in full, not once but twice."I am acutely conscious of the cost it has had for them."Last year I offered an unreserved apology for the abuse of power and leadership that took place within the Nine O'Clock Service. Today's verdict adds to that same picture, and my apology stands in full."Lawyer Richard Scorer, who is representing the women in civil action against the Church of England, called Brain a "serial abuser"."But we mustn't forget that he was fast-tracked to ordination, supported, promoted and protected by the Church of England," he added."A full accounting of their role in this appalling saga is long overdue and must now follow."Julie Moss, senior crown prosecutor for Yorkshire and Humberside, said Brain had perpetrated "a disturbing campaign of manipulation and abuse".She added: "Victims were isolated from their loved ones, made financially and emotionally dependent on the group, and made to believe that resistance to Brain's sexual advances reflected their own personal or spiritual failings."Det Supt Eleanor Welsh, of South Yorkshire Police, said: "These women have waited three or four decades for these verdicts and bravely relived their ordeals in a bid to secure justice."Judge Freya Newbury said victims would be given the chance to deliver impact statements at a sentencing hearing, which is likely to take two days.

schema.headline: Former priest Chris Brain guilty of raping and assaulting women
